test_recorded_numerical_schema_is_not_the_task_or_model_interpretation_form[None-literature_channel_cells-channel_cells_schema-Determine what the reported membrane-current or ion-release experiment establishes about the studied molecule's transport activity and ion specificity. Identify the actual organism, protein construct, preparation, membrane system, ion composition, experimental arrangement and measured endpoint. Distinguish purified reconstitution from cellular measurements. Establish whether compared molecules replace one another or coexist; preserve additional changes beyond the intended variable.

For electrical measurements, identify whether each value is a signed current, current-step magnitude, applied voltage, reversal voltage, reported conductance or occupancy measurement. Preserve the voltage convention, grounded side, ion gradient and baseline definition. Keep salt-gradient and biionic measurements distinct. A common paper or protein name does not establish that two operands belong to the same measurement arrangement.

Establish what the observed unit represents. Distinguish a protein-containing insertion packet, a conducting unit, a polypeptide and a pore. Preserve unresolved oligomer or pore assignments. Do not turn event counts, bilayer counts, time points or histogram samples into independent protein preparations.

For ion-release measurements, distinguish accumulated release, a normalized release fraction and an initial flux. Identify initial, plateau and detergent-release measurements where available. Preserve dead time, detection limits, assumed vesicle dimensions and reported approximations. A response faster than instrument dead time supplies a limitation or bound, not an observed initial rate.

Examine whether the signal is attributable to the intended protein and ion. A closed-channel baseline is not a protein-free membrane control. Electrical current measures charge flow; converting it into flux of a specified ion requires the applicable charge and attribution relationship. Keep mixed contributions and missing controls explicit. Complementary electrical and chemical measurements can address different weaknesses without becoming independent replication automatically.

Preserve reported uncertainty, its declared meaning, independent preparation identities and shared measurements. Do not reinterpret an unspecified spread as SD, SEM or known sampling variance. Use covariance only with established measurement ownership. Occupancy and current amplitude may be combined only when their joint experimental meaning supports that calculation; preserve substates and missing joint relationships.

Nominate source-supported operands and their experimental relationships. Leave parsing, unit conversion and arithmetic to deterministic readers and calculators. Preserve reported and calculated values separately, including disagreements. Return the requested numerical components with their conditions, uncertainty, dependencies and unresolved limitations. Do not invent an overall reliability grade, annotation probability, target-transfer weight or missing value.-literature_channel_work]

test_recorded_numerical_schema_is_not_the_task_or_model_interpretation_form[None-literature_compiled_assay_cells-compiled_assay_cells_schema-Evaluate what the selected experimental measurements establish about the studied molecule's measured activity and the functional assertion under investigation. Identify the actual molecule, construct, preparation, experimental system, endpoint, conditions and intended variable. Use source-supported context already available or examine the relevant source when needed. A function may emerge from the investigation; an initial candidate annotation is not required.

Select the saved numerical components that answer the assigned question. Establish each component's physical meaning, units, denominator and relationship to the particular assay. Matching names, units or publication do not establish applicability. Preserve the distinction between the directly measured endpoint and the asserted molecular function, including unresolved reporter-to-product relationships.

Determine which corrections have already been applied. Distinguish sample-minus-blank rate from gross signal, separately measured contamination from background already removed, instrument recovery from an enzyme-spike response, and total-molecule amount from active-site amount. Do not repeat subtraction, calibration or normalization already incorporated in a measurement. Preserve incompatible measurements as useful evidence while leaving the unsupported combined result unavailable.

Examine comparability outside the intended change and isolation of the measured effect separately. A condition-control response must address the relevant nuisance difference while excluding the variable deliberately tested. Establish whether compared molecules replace one another or coexist. Preserve additional changes, mixed contributors and alternative explanations rather than treating a control label as proof of isolation.

Preserve the underlying measurement owners and shared inputs across components. A calculated recovery ratio depends on its measured and nominal standards; a net optical rate can share background, calibration or path-length inputs with other results. Do not treat derived quantities as independent because they appear in different sections. Retain reported uncertainty and replication meanings; select covariance and a sampling model only when supported.

Nominate the applicable saved operands, experimental relationships and correction stages. Deterministic functions perform validation, unit conversion and arithmetic. Retain usable partial results when a relationship, measurement or required implementation is missing, and distinguish those reasons. Return only the requested numerical sections and their necessary qualifications. Do not invent missing controls, a universal quality grade, function probability, target-transfer weight or cross-assay total.-literature_compiled_assay_work]
